title: Register halving computation
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with designated register $r$ and states $h_R,h_0,h_F,h_T,next$. Suppose its transitions at these states implement the stated end-marker and leftward halving actions for each possible scanned symbol, and none of these four states is a call state. For every configuration $c$ and natural number $n$, there is a time $T$ at which the program, started in state $h_R$ with register $r$ containing the binary word for $n$ and its head at zero, reaches state $next$ with that register containing the binary word for $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ and its head at zero. At every earlier time $t<T$, its configuration differs from $c$ only in the state, tape, and head position of register $r$; the state is not a call state and the head position lies between $-1$ and the length of the binary word for $n$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: A register program $P$, oracle, input, register $r$, and states $h_R,h_0,h_F,h_T,next$.
At $h_R$, every transition is the specified end-marker action.
At $h_0,h_F,h_T$, every transition is the specified halving action for the scanned symbol.
None of $h_R,h_0,h_F,h_T$ is a call state.
